newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia sees Hashimoto visit before year-end.
newsitem.headline: Russia sees Hashimoto visit before year-end.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin may have an informal weekend meeting with Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto in the Russian Far East or Siberia before the end of the year, the Kremlin spokesman said on Wednesday.
Spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky told a news conference the two men had agreed to begin regular meetings at last weekend's Group of Seven summit in Denver, United States.
Yastrzhembsky said the Denver talks had created a "qualitatively new" spirit in Russian-Japanese relations.

"There is obviously a change for the better in Russian-Japanese relations," he said, adding that it was already bearing fruit in the form of a deal to be signed in the next few days granting Japan rights to catch 26,000 tonnes of salmon in Russian coastal waters next year.

Asked about Yeltsin's offer in Denver to stop aiming nuclear missiles at Japan, Yastrzhembsky said: "This requires a presidential order. I think the order will be issued. The defence minister knows about the conversation. I think it will be a matter of days."
